The '''Territorial Settlement of 1951''' was the border component of the postwar order created after the [[Avant Great War]] and [[Continuation War]]. It attempted to resolve the status of former Vesperan territories, liberated states, occupation zones, and disputed claims.

== Background ==

The collapse of the [[Vesperan Empire]] in 1949 created overlapping claims across former imperial territories. Some regions declared independence, some required occupation, and others were claimed by states that had fought in the war.

The settlement was connected to the broader [[Treaty Accord of 1951]] and the later Istragarde framework.

== Belcanto And Khalindar ==

For the [[Belcanto Nations]], the settlement resolved many borders after independence. For Khalindar, it became a source of grievance because some promised territories were not transferred to the empire.

Belcanto source material says the settlement resolved most border issues while leaving disputes with Khalindar regarding promised territories. This made the settlement a direct bridge between the postwar order and the later [[Khalindarian reparations dispute]].

== Legacy ==

The settlement stabilized many new borders but did not create a strong enforcement system. Its unresolved claims continued to shape diplomacy and conflict throughout the late twentieth century.
